I wish I could tell her what became of the boy she rescued from that back room. I wish I could show her this book and say: This is what you made possible. This is what emerged. Absent of finding her, I offer this instead: a dedication, and a story, and the hope that somewhere she knows that her work mattered—that a thesis written in 1973 about a newly understood condition called dyslexia changed the trajectory of a life and, perhaps, contributed in some small way to the development of next-generation learning tools. The letters still move sometimes, even now. But I happily wait for meaning to emerge. If you would like to engage in the conversation with Claude AI from the book, scan this QR Code. OceanofPDF.com ABOUT THE AUTHOR Bob Burgin is a serial venture capital and private equity–backed entrepreneur who has spent the last thirty-five years “extrapolating scientific research findings into products.” Since 2010, he has served as chairman and CEO of Amplifire, a company working to advance human learning. His mission has been to collaborate with leading brain scientists to “uncover how our brains encode, store, and retrieve new learning in order to build hyper-efficient learning systems.” In his work, he has been deeply influenced by and collaborated with pioneers in the science of learning, including Dr. Robert Bjork, Dr. Daniel Schacter, and Dr. Henry Roediger III. Bob’s work is driven by the realization that his team was “trying to reverse-engineer one of evolution’s greatest achievements: how a twenty-watt brain creates lasting knowledge.” The learning products that result from this work are widely deployed in high-stakes environments, where they serve many of the largest healthcare systems in the United States. For the past nine years, Bob and his team have been working on integrating these breakthroughs in human learning with rapidly improving artificial intelligence (AI) to develop an advanced and hyperscalable conversational AI training capability. Bob and the team hold three patents in conversational AI training integrated with advanced brain science, dating back to 2017. Prior to his work in human learning, Bob was the founder and CEO of a company that, in the early days of the internet, built web-based customer service agents, working closely with groundbreaking Stanford researchers Clifford Nass and Byron Reeves to understand the “media equation” and human–computer interaction. He eventually sold that company to the world’s largest customer service outsourcing company. Bob does not identify as a research scientist but rather as a connective thread —a storyteller who maps insights from diverse fields to find perspective.
